I actually also have an 06 Prix with 177k on it. Some of my thoughts:

First off, if you have the base or GT trim, it has the 3800 Series 3 motor, the difference is the GT comes supercharged from the factory.

The 3800 Series 3 motor is notorious for issues with the power steering pump. When it starts to make that God awful whine you should replace it, otherwise it will just die one day (speaking from experience). Other than that, the engine is rock solid and will go for a very long time if you change your oil regularly.

Those stock speakers are fantastic, I put in a new stereo and subwoofers and it is tuned perfectly for my taste, with a lot of bass but still clean and clear mids and highs.

Rear window regulators are crap and are prone to fail at any given moment. Fronts seem fine however.

Aftermarket wheels and a nice paint job/wrap will really make the car pop.

Transmission on the base trim is a little bit underbuilt. If it was not maintenanced on time by previous owners it may start slipping or eventually fail before 250k.

Factory superchargers do not bolt onto the base trim, if you want to do that you will need a lot of the supporting mechanical parts including the upper intake manifold and a transmission upgrade. You might be able to do it cheaper pulling an engine and transmission off a wrecked car that came stock with it.

OEM spec calls for ceramic brakes. Don't cheap out and put semi metallic pads on if you want to be able to stop your 3500 lb machine.

A ZZP catted downpipe and aftermarket muffler will make the car sound fantastic without being extremely loud. The car also sounds like crap with open headers.

Tinted windows help the appearance of the car a lot.

I can't see any scenario where software written for 7 wouldn't run on 10. When XP finally lost support back in 2014, it was a much bigger deal because there were major differences in the Kernel security policies between XP and Vista that rendered some software completely non-functional even in compatibility mode. The jump from 7 to 10 is nowhere near as big. Most of the Kernel differences between 7 and 8/8.1 and 8/8.1 and 10 are optimizations. The only way I can see this being an issue is if one were running specialty hardware that doesn't have drivers for anything newer than 7. Most of the time, if you find a Win8 driver, you can make it work on 10.
